label: thm:intro-affine
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:intro-affine} Assume that $\operatorname{char}k=p>2$. 
There is a Frobenius splitting of $S$ compatible with every $S_u$.
For every $u\leq w^\bullet$, the coordinate ring $k[S_u]$ is strongly
$F$-regular.
head: environment

label: thm:intro-embeddings
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:intro-embeddings} Assume that $\operatorname{char}k=p>2$. 
Let $X$ be any equivariant embedding of $S$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*]
\item $X$ admits a Frobenius splitting compatible with every boundary
      divisor and every $X_u$.
\item Every $X_u$ is strongly $F$-regular.
\item If $X$ is projective, every $X_u$ is globally $F$-regular.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: thm:intro-zero
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:intro-zero}
Assume that $\operatorname{char}k=0$ and let $X$ be an equivariant
embedding of $S$. Every $X_u$ is of strongly $F$-regular type; in
particular, it is normal, Cohen--Macaulay, and has rational singularities.
If $X$ is projective, every $X_u$ is of globally $F$-regular type.
head: environment

label: prop:intro-closed-orbit
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:intro-closed-orbit}\label{Prop:D}
Assume that $\operatorname{char}k\neq2$. Let $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$ be the wonderful
compactification of the associated adjoint symmetric space
$S_{\mathrm{ad}}$, with closed orbit $Y\cong G/P_{\mathbf{I}_\bullet}$.
For every $u\leq w^\bullet$, the scheme-theoretic intersection
$\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_u\cap Y$ is a reduced union of projected Richardson varieties.
Moreover, $\bigcup_{i\in\mathbf{I}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_{s_i}\cap Y)$ is the union of all
projected Richardson divisors of $Y$.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md: We call the stratum $\mathring S_u$ the \emph{(open) double Bruhat cell} for the symmetric space $G/K$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Let $\widetilde G=G\times G$. We consider the involution
\[
\widetilde\theta:G\times G\to G\times G,
\qquad
(g,h)\longmapsto(\theta(h),\theta(g)).
\]
Denote the fixed-point group by $\widetilde K=\widetilde G^{\widetilde\theta}$. Consider the symmetric space $\widetilde G/\widetilde K$. It follows from Evens--Lu \cite{EL06} that the intersections of diagonal $G$-orbits with $(B^+,B^-)$-orbits are precisely the $T$-leaves of the natural Poisson structure on $\widetilde G/\widetilde K$ as a Poisson homogeneous space; see also Lu \cite{Lu14}. The map
\[
G\times G\to G,
\qquad
(g,h)\longmapsto g\theta(h)^{-1}
\]
induces an isomorphism $\widetilde G/\widetilde K\cong G$. Under this isomorphism, diagonal $G$-orbits in $\widetilde G/\widetilde K$ are identified with the twisted conjugacy classes, and $(B^+,B^-)$-orbits are identified with $(B^+,\theta(B^-))$ double cosets in $G$. Under this isomorphism, $S$ is precisely the diagonal $G$-orbit of $\widetilde K$. This leads to the stratum $\mathring S_u$.
head: environment

label: lem:prelim-strata-intersection
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove Part~(1). Let $\theta'=\operatorname{Int}(\dot w^\bullet)\theta$. Then $\theta'$ fixes $B^+$ and $B^-$. Let $C$ be the $\theta'$-twisted conjugacy class of $(\dot w^\bullet)^{-1}$. Then $\iota(G/K)=C\cdot\dot w^\bullet$. Since $B^+K/K\subset G/K$ is dense, $B^+(\dot w^\bullet)^{-1}B^+\cap C$ is dense in $C$. By \cite{CLT10}*{Section 2.4}, the intersection 
\[
C\cap B^+\dot uB^-=(\iota(G/K)\cap B^+\dot uB^-\dot w^\bullet)(\dot w^\bullet)^{-1}
\]
is non-empty if and only if $u\leq w^\bullet=(w^\bullet)^{-1}$.

We prove Part~(2). We follow the notation in the preceding remark. By the Bruhat decomposition, we have
\[
\overline{B^+\dot uB^-\dot w^\bullet}
=
\bigsqcup_{u\leq v}B^+\dot vB^-\dot w^\bullet.
\]
We can equivalently consider the closure relations in $\widetilde G/\widetilde K$, since $S$ is closed in $G$. Then we can apply Richardson's theorem. In particular,
\[
S_u
=
S\cap \iota^{-1}(\overline{B^+\dot uB^-\dot w^\bullet})
=
\bigsqcup_{u\leq v\leq w^\bullet}\mathring S_v.
\]
The finiteness condition in Richardson's theorem is not needed here, since $S$ is closed; see \cite{Ri92}*{Theorem 2.1}. The assertions about smoothness, connectedness, and dimension in Part~(3) follow from \cite{Ri92}*{Corollary 1.5}. Finally, $B^+\dot uB^-\dot w^\bullet$ is affine, and $\iota(\mathring S_u)$ is closed in this double Bruhat cell. Hence $\mathring S_u$ is affine.

label: thm:gloFre
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:gloFre}
Let $P$ be an irreducible projective variety over $k$. The following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\arabic*)}]
\item $P$ is globally $F$-regular.
\item The variety $P$ is stably Frobenius split along an ample effective Cartier divisor $D$, and $P\setminus D$ is strongly $F$-regular.
\item The variety $P$ is stably Frobenius split along every effective Cartier divisor.
\end{enumerate}

label: rem:adjoint-spherical-lattice
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:adjoint-spherical-lattice}
The inclusion $\breve X_{\mathrm{ad}}\subseteq\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}\cap Q$
need not be an equality. For $G=\mathrm{SL}_2$ with
$\theta(g)=(g^t)^{-1}$, let $\omega$ be the fundamental weight, so
$\alpha=2\omega$ and $\theta(\omega)=-\omega$. Then
\[
\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}=2\mathbb Z\omega=Q,
\qquad
\breve X_{\mathrm{ad}}=2\mathbb Z\alpha=2Q
\subsetneq\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}\cap Q.
\]
This discrepancy is a combinatorial shadow of the fact that $H$ may be strictly bigger than $KZ(G)$.
In this example, $Z(G)\subset K$ and $H/K\simeq\mu_2$.

title: Remark
body_md:
In our previous work \cite{BS25b}, we use the full filtered piece $k[S_{\mathrm{sc}}]_{\preceq\lambda}$ in degree
$\lambda$. Our $E_\lambda$ retains only the component with right
$D$-character $[\lambda]$. This character condition implements the
diagonal $D$-quotient needed for the adjoint symmetric space.

label: lem:enveloping-order
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:enveloping-order}
Let $\lambda,\nu\in\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}$. Then
\[
[\lambda]=[\nu]
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\lambda-\nu\in\breve X_{\mathrm{ad}}.
\]
If $\nu\preceq\lambda$, these conditions are equivalent to
$\lambda-\nu\in Q_\theta^+$, and then $\nu\leq\lambda$.
Consequently,
\[
E_\lambda=\bigl(k[S_{\mathrm{sc}}]_{\leq\lambda}\bigr)_{[\lambda]},
\]
and $E_\lambda$ has a good filtration with factors $V(\nu)^*$ for
$\nu\in\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}^+$ such that
$\lambda-\nu\in Q_\theta^+$, each occurring once.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The first equivalence follows from \eqref{eq:enveloping-D}.
Suppose $\nu\preceq\lambda$ and $[\lambda]=[\nu]$. Then
$\lambda-\nu\in\breve X_{\mathrm{ad}}\subset Q$, so
$\nu\leq\lambda$. By \cite{BS25b}*{Lemma 2.3},
$\lambda-\nu$ lies in the nonnegative rational cone generated by
the $\overline\alpha_i$. Since these form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of
$\breve X_{\mathrm{ad}}$, its coefficients are nonnegative integers.
Thus $\lambda-\nu\in Q_\theta^+$. The converse follows from
$Q_\theta^+\subset\breve X_{\mathrm{ad}}$.

The good-filtration factor $V(\nu)^*$ of
$k[S_{\mathrm{sc}}]$ is indecomposable, and the $D$-action commutes
with $G$. It therefore has a single $D$-character, namely $[\nu]$,
as its $B^-$-eigenline is represented by $\chi_\nu$.
Exactness of character spaces and the preceding
equivalence therefore retain precisely the factors with
$\lambda-\nu\in Q_\theta^+$. These are also the factors of
$\bigl(k[S_{\mathrm{sc}}]_{\leq\lambda}\bigr)_{[\lambda]}$,
proving the asserted equality.
head: environment

label: thm:enveloping-quotient
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:enveloping-quotient}
The semistable and stable loci in $\widehat E$ coincide and are
independent of the regular spherical weight $\eta$. Denote this
common locus by $\widehat E^0$. The geometric quotient
\[
\widehat E^0/\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}=\mathbf X_\eta
\]
is the wonderful compactification $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$ of $S_{\mathrm{ad}}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The argument of \cite{BS25b}*{Theorem 4.10} applies with the weight
monoid
\[
\{(\nu,\lambda)\in\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}^+
\times\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}\mid\lambda-\nu\in Q_\theta^+\}. \qedhere
\]

label: rem:affine-embedding-constructions
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:affine-embedding-constructions}
Although $\widehat S$ need not be a symmetric space for
$G\times\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}$ in the fixed-point-subgroup sense,
the constructions of affine embeddings, their orbit closures, and
dual canonical bases in \cite{BS25b}*{Sections 3.1--3.3 and 4.2}
apply with the character condition $[\nu]=[\lambda]$.
The essential point is that, within each character class,
Lemma \ref{lem:enveloping-order} identifies the order
$\lambda-\nu\in Q_\theta^+$ with ordinary dominance, which defines
the dual-canonical-basis filtration. One uses the corresponding
character components and the same constructions by closed
saturated submonoids and ideals. We omit the details, since they
repeat the arguments of \cite{BS25b} with this restriction.

label: prop:wc
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:wc}
\begin{enumerate}
\item The lattice $\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}$ is contained in $\operatorname{Pic}(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace)$.
                                                                                        
\item The canonical sheaf is
\[
\omega_\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace\cong\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_{\overline\rho+\sum_{i\in\mathbf{I}_\circ'}\overline\alpha_i},
\qquad \rho=\sum_{i\in\mathbf{I}}\omega_i.
\]
\item The boundary is
\[
\partial\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace=\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace\setminus S_{\mathrm{ad}}=\bigcup_{i\in\mathbf{I}_\circ'}D_i,
\qquad \ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace(D_i)\cong\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_{-\overline\alpha_i},
\]
where each $D_i$ is a $G$-stable prime divisor.
\item The intersection $\bigcap_{i\in\mathbf{I}_\circ'}D_i$ is the unique closed
$G$-orbit, isomorphic to $G/P$, where $P\supset B^+$ is the standard
parabolic subgroup associated with $\mathbf{I}_\bullet$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: lem:Ttorsor
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Ttorsor}
The quotient morphism
\[
\pi:\widehat E^0\longrightarrow\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace
\]
is a Zariski-locally trivial $\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}$-torsor.
More precisely, every $x\in\widehat E^0$ has a $\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}$-stable affine
neighbourhood of the form
\[
\pi^{-1}(W)\cong W\times \breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}
\]
over an affine open subset $W\subset\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that $q_\eta=\chi_\eta e^\eta\in k[\widehat E]$ and that
$D(gq_\eta)$, for $g\in G(k)$, cover $\widehat E^0$.
For $\lambda\in\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}^+$, put
$q_\lambda=\chi_\lambda e^\lambda$.
We first prove that the scheme-theoretic stabilizers are trivial.
For any $\nu\in\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}$, choose $n$ sufficiently
large that $n\eta\pm\nu\in\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}^+$. On
$D(q_\eta)$, the functions
\[
q_\nu=\frac{q_{n\eta+\nu}}{q_\eta^n},\qquad
q_{-\nu}=\frac{q_{n\eta-\nu}}{q_\eta^n}
\]
are regular and homogeneous of degrees $\nu$ and $-\nu$.
Multiplicativity of the eigenfunctions gives
\[
q_{n\eta+\nu}q_{n\eta-\nu}=q_{2n\eta}=q_\eta^{2n},
\]
so $q_\nu q_{-\nu}=1$. Thus both functions are units on
$D(q_\eta)$.

Let $x$ be a geometric point of $D(q_\eta)$, and let
$N=\operatorname{Stab}_{\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}}(x)$ be its
scheme-theoretic stabilizer. The homogeneity identity
$q_\nu(xt)=\nu(t)q_\nu(x)$ restricts to
\[
q_\nu(x)\,\nu|_N=q_\nu(x)
\]
as an equality of regular functions on $N$. Since $q_\nu(x)$ is
an invertible scalar, $\nu|_N=1$. This holds for every
$\nu\in\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}$. In particular, for a basis
$\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_r$ of this lattice, we have
\[
N\subseteq\bigcap_{j=1}^r\ker(\varepsilon_j)=\{1\}
\]
as group schemes, and hence $N$ is trivial. The $G$-action
commutes with the torus action, so the same holds on every
$D(gq_\eta)$. These opens cover $\widehat E^0$.

Let $x\in\widehat E^0$. Triviality of its stabilizer means that the
degrees of homogeneous functions nonzero at $x$ generate $\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}$.
Choose finitely many such functions $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in k[\widehat E]$.
Since $x$ is semistable, also choose $h\in k[\widehat E]_{n\eta}$ with
$h(x)\ne0$, for some $n>0$, and set $F=hf_1\cdots f_m$.
Then $D(F)$ is $\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}$-stable, contains $x$, and is contained in
$\widehat E^0$. Each $f_i$ is a unit in $k[\widehat E]_F$.
For a basis $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_r$ of $\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}$, choose
Laurent monomials $u_j$ in the $f_i$ of degree $\varepsilon_j$.
Writing $B=(k[\widehat E]_F)_0$, multiplication gives an isomorphism
of graded algebras
\[
B\otimes_k k[\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}]\xrightarrow{\sim}k[\widehat E]_F,
\qquad b\otimes e^{\sum_jn_j\varepsilon_j}
\longmapsto b\prod_j u_j^{n_j}.
\]
Indeed, dividing a homogeneous element by the unit of its degree
leaves an element of $B$, and uniqueness follows from the grading.

Since $\pi$ is a geometric quotient, the stable open $D(F)$ is
saturated and $W=\pi(D(F))$ is open. Its affine quotient is
$W=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The displayed isomorphism therefore gives
\[
\pi^{-1}(W)=D(F)\cong W\times \breve T_{\mathrm{sc}},
\]
with $\pi$ equal to the first projection.
head: environment

label: lem:codim2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:codim2}
The complement $\widehat E\setminus\widehat E^0$ has codimension
at least two. Consequently, restriction induces an isomorphism
\[
k[\widehat E]\xrightarrow{\sim}
\Gamma(\widehat E^0,\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_{\widehat E^0}).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first apply the orbit argument to the variety
$\widetilde E$. An irreducible component of
$\widetilde E\setminus\widetilde E^0$ is stable under the connected
group $G\times \breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}$. By \cite{BS25b}*{Proposition 4.9}, its prime
ideal is $\mathfrak p_{J_1,J_2}$ for an essential pair
$(J_1,J_2)$. The instability criterion in
\cite{BS25b}*{Theorem 4.10} gives $J_1\ne\mathbf{I}_\circ'$, and essentiality
forces $J_2\ne\mathbf{I}_\circ'$. The defining faces in
\cite{BS25b}*{Definition 4.7} give strict inclusions
\[
(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p_{\mathbf{I}_\circ',J_2}
\subsetneq\mathfrak p_{J_1,J_2}.
\]
The first inclusion is strict because a boundary direction
$(0,\overline\alpha_j)$ with $j\notin J_2$ lies in the first nonzero ideal.
The second is strict because a positive multiple of
$(\overline\omega_i,\overline\omega_i)$ with $i\notin J_1$ lies
in the latter ideal but not the former. Thus the unstable
complement in $\widetilde E$ has codimension at least two.

The finite surjective morphism $q_D:\widetilde E\to\widehat E$
satisfies $q_D^{-1}(\widehat E^0)=\widetilde E^0$. It preserves
dimensions of closed subsets and maps the unstable complement
onto $\widehat E\setminus\widehat E^0$, proving the same
codimension bound for $\widehat E$. The restriction isomorphism
then follows from normality of $\widehat E$.
head: environment

label: thm:linebundles
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:linebundles}
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\mu\in \breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}$, the associated bundle
\[
\widehat E^0\times^{\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}}k_\mu\longrightarrow\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace,
\qquad (x,a)t=(xt,\mu(t)^{-1}a),
\]
is isomorphic to $\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_\mu$.
\item There are multiplication-compatible identifications
\[
H^0(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_\mu)
\cong k[\widehat E]^{(-\mu)}
=E_{-\mu}e^{-\mu}
\cong\bigl(k[S_{\mathrm{sc}}]_{\leq-\mu}\bigr)_{[-\mu]}.
\]
Here the superscript $(-\mu)$ denotes the semi-invariant functions
satisfying $F(xt)=\mu(t)^{-1}F(x)$.
\item If $0\ne\phi\in E_\mu$ corresponds to
$s_\phi\in H^0(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_{-\mu})$, then
\[
\pi^{-1}\bigl(Z(s_\phi)\bigr)
=Z(\phi e^\mu)\cap\widehat E^0
\]
as closed subschemes. Consequently, the zero scheme, and hence the
divisor, of $s_\phi$ is the scheme-theoretic image of this inverse
image under $\pi$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma \ref{lem:Ttorsor} makes the associated bundle invertible.
On the chart $D(q_\eta)$, the homogeneous unit $q_\lambda$ gives
a nowhere vanishing section of the bundle with index $-\lambda$.
Its left $B^-$-weight is $-\lambda$, so its value at the $T$-fixed
point $eP$ of the closed orbit has fiber character $-\lambda$.
Injectivity of restriction to $G/P$
\cite{DCS99}*{Theorem 4.2(ii)} identifies this bundle with
$\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_{-\lambda}$, proving (1).

A section of the associated bundle with index $\mu$ is a regular
function $F$ on $\widehat E^0$ with $F(xt)=\mu(t)^{-1}F(x)$.
Lemma \ref{lem:codim2} identifies these functions with the
degree $-\mu$ component of $k[\widehat E]$.
Lemma \ref{lem:enveloping-order} then gives (2); multiplication is
the multiplication of semi-invariant functions.

For (3), on a trivializing chart $W$, choose a homogeneous unit
$u_\mu$ of degree $\mu$ on $\pi^{-1}(W)$. Write
$\phi e^\mu=(\pi^*a)u_\mu$ for $a\in\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace(W)$.
The section $s_\phi|_W$ is represented by $a$, and $u_\mu$ is
invertible, so the asserted equality holds scheme-theoretically.
The charts cover $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$, and faithful flatness of $\pi$ identifies
the scheme-theoretic image with $Z(s_\phi)$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
If there are exceptional roots in the sense of \cite{DCS99}*{Section~4}, the lattice $\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}$ need not be all of
$\operatorname{Pic}(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace)$. Such additional classes require
semi-invariant functions on $G$, rather than functions on $G/K$.

label: prop:chart-richardson
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:chart-richardson}
Let $v\le w^\bullet$ and $\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}=T/T^\theta$.
The chart parametrizations
\[
\begin{aligned}
U_P^-\times\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}&\xrightarrow{\sim}B^-K/K,
&(x,tT^\theta)&\longmapsto xtK,\\
U_P^+\times\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}&\xrightarrow{\sim}B^+K/K,
&(x,tT^\theta)&\longmapsto x\dot w^\bullet tK
\end{aligned}
\]
induce the isomorphisms
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathring S_v\cap(B^-K/K)
&\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathring{\mathcal{R}}_{w_\bullet,vw_0}\times\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}},\\
xtK&\longmapsto (x\dot w_\bullet B^+,tT^\theta),\\[4pt]
\mathring S_v\cap(B^+K/K)
&\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathring{\mathcal{R}}_{\kappa(v),w^\bullet}\times\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}},\\
x\dot w^\bullet tK&\longmapsto (x\dot w^\bullet B^+,tT^\theta).
\end{aligned}
\]
                                                               
    
                 
                                                 
                                                                             
               
    

(The corresponding
statements hold on the adjoint symmetric space as well. )
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The $U_P^-\times\breve T_{\mathrm{sc}}$ chart
parametrization is the local structure theorem
\cite{DCS99}*{Proposition~3.8}. Its $\dot w^\bullet$-translate
has unipotent coordinate $U_P^+$ and is the open $B^+$-orbit
$B^+K/K$, giving the other parametrization.

For $x\in U_P^-$, one has $\theta(x)^{-1}\in U_P^+
\subset\theta(B^-)$. Therefore
\begin{align*}
xtK\in\mathring S_v
&\Longleftrightarrow
xt\theta(t)^{-1}\theta(x)^{-1}
\in B^+\dot v\dot w^\bullet\theta(B^-)\\
&\Longleftrightarrow x\in B^+\dot v\dot w^\bullet\theta(B^-)\\
&\Longleftrightarrow x\dot w_\bullet\in B^+\dot v\dot w_0B^+.
\end{align*}
Here the torus factors are absorbed into $\theta(B^-)$.
The map $x\mapsto x\dot w_\bullet B^+$ identifies $U_P^-$
with $B^-\dot w_\bullet B^+/B^+$, proving the first restriction.

For $x\in U_P^+$, the identity $\theta(w^\bullet)=w^\bullet$
gives
\[
\iota(x\dot w^\bullet tK)=x\,a(t)\,\theta(x)^{-1},
\qquad a(t)=\dot w^\bullet t\theta(t)^{-1}
\theta(\dot w^\bullet)^{-1}\in T.
\]
Absorbing the left $B^+$-factors, and then applying inversion
and $\theta$, yields
\begin{align*}
x\dot w^\bullet tK\in\mathring S_v
&\Longleftrightarrow
\theta(x)^{-1}(\dot w^\bullet)^{-1}\in B^+\dot vB^-\\
&\Longleftrightarrow
\dot w^\bullet\theta(x)\in B^-\dot v^{-1}B^+\\
&\Longleftrightarrow
x\dot w^\bullet\in B^-\dot{\kappa(v)}B^+.
\end{align*}
For the last equivalence, conjugate the $\theta$-image by
$\dot w^\bullet$ and use
\[
(w^\bullet)^{-1}\theta(v^{-1})w^\bullet
=w_0\tau(v^{-1})w_0=\kappa(v).
\]
Factors in $T$ arising from the chosen representatives do not
affect these double cosets. We conclude that  $x\dot w^\bullet B^+ \in \mathring{\mathcal{R}}_{\kappa(v),w^\bullet}$.

label: le:flo
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $f\in k[G]$, write $\text{wt}(f)=(\lambda,\nu)\in X\times X$ if
$f(t_1^{-1}gt_2)=\lambda(t_1)\nu(t_2)f(g)$ for $t_1,t_2\in T$.
For $f\in k[S_{\mathrm{sc}}]$, write $\text{wt}_\theta(f)=\lambda$ if
$f(t^{-1}gK)=\lambda(t)f(gK)$ for $t\in T$.
Then
\[
\text{wt}_\theta(\iota^*f)=\lambda+\theta\nu
\qquad\text{when }\text{wt}(f)=(\lambda,\nu)
\]
whenever the pullback is nonzero.

Recall that $k[G]_{\le\mu}$ has a good $G\times G$-filtration
with sections $V(\gamma)^*\boxtimes V(-w_0\gamma)^*$ for
$\gamma\in X^+$, $\gamma\le\mu$. If $f\in k[G]_{\le\mu}$
has weight $(\lambda,\nu)$, then
\[
-\mu\le x\lambda,\qquad x\nu\le\mu\qquad(x\in W).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\text{wt}_\theta(\iota^*f)=\lambda-w_\bullet\tau\nu
\ge-\mu-\tau\mu.
\]
Thus every weight of $M:=\iota^*(k[G]_{\le\mu})$ is at least
$-\mu-\tau\mu$.

We first prove the following assertion.

\emph{(a) Let $\lambda\in\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}$, and write
$\lambda=\sum_{i\in\mathbf{I}}n_i\alpha_i$, with $n_i\in\mathbb Q$.
If $n_i\ge0$ for $i\in\mathbf{I}_\circ$, then $n_i\ge0$ for every
$i\in\mathbf{I}$.}

Write $\lambda=\lambda_\circ+\lambda_\bullet$, where
\[
\lambda_\circ\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0}[\alpha_i\mid i\in\mathbf{I}_\circ],
\qquad
\lambda_\bullet\in\mathbb Q[\alpha_i\mid i\in\mathbf{I}_\bullet].
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_\circ'=w_\bullet\tau\lambda_\circ-\tau\lambda_\circ
\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0}[\alpha_i\mid i\in\mathbf{I}_\bullet].
\]
Since $\theta$ fixes the black roots,
$\theta\lambda=-\tau\lambda_\circ-\lambda_\circ'+\lambda_\bullet$.
Comparing black-root coefficients in $\theta\lambda=-\lambda$
gives $2\lambda_\bullet=\lambda_\circ'$. This proves~(a).

We next prove:

\emph{(b) If $\lambda\in\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}$ and
$\lambda\le\mu+\tau\mu$, then $\lambda\le\overline\mu$.}

Put $\delta=\overline\mu-\lambda\in\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}$.
Since
\[
\overline\mu-(\mu+\tau\mu)
=w_\bullet\tau\mu-\tau\mu
\in\mathbb Z[\alpha_i\mid i\in\mathbf{I}_\bullet],
\]
one has $\delta\in Q$, and the white-root coefficients of
$\delta$ equal those of $\mu+\tau\mu-\lambda$, hence are
nonnegative. By~(a), all simple-root coefficients of $\delta$
are nonnegative. They are integers because $\delta\in Q$.
Thus $\lambda\le\overline\mu$, proving~(b).

Return to $M$. Choose a total order
$\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\ldots$ on $\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}^+$
refining dominance, with the finite downward-closed set
\[
\{\gamma\in\breve X_{\mathrm{sc}}^+\mid\gamma\le\overline\mu\}
\]
first. Put
$F_N=\sum_{k=1}^N k[S_{\mathrm{sc}}]_{\le\gamma_k}$.
By \cite{BS24}*{Theorem~4.9}, with the right-quotient convention,
$F_N/F_{N-1}\cong V(\gamma_N)^*$.
If $M=0$ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, let $N$ be minimal
such that $M\subseteq F_N$, and consider its image $M_N$ under
\[
F_N\longrightarrow F_N/F_{N-1}\cong V(\gamma_N)^*.
\]
The subspace $M$ is $G$-stable for the twisted diagonal action,
so $M_N$ is a nonzero $G$-submodule. It contains a vector of weight
$-\gamma_N$: its dual is a nonzero quotient of $V(\gamma_N)$,
in which the highest weight generator must survive.
The preliminary weight bound gives $\gamma_N\le\mu+\tau\mu$.
Applying~(b) to the spherical label $\gamma_N$ yields
$\gamma_N\le\overline\mu$. By the chosen order, every
$\gamma_k$ with $k\le N$ also satisfies this inequality.
Therefore
\[
M\subseteq F_N\subseteq k[S_{\mathrm{sc}}]_{\le\overline\mu},
\]
as required.

label: prop:dv
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:dv}
(1) For $i\in\mathbf{I}$, the element $\overline{\varphi_i}\in H^0(G/P,\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_{-\overline{\omega_i}})$ is nonzero.

    (2) For $i\in\mathbf{I}_\circ$, one has $Z(\overline{\varphi_i})=\overline{B^-s_iP/P}\cup \overline{B^+w_0s_{\tau i}P/P} $.

    (3) For $i\in \mathbf{I}_\bullet$, one has $Z(\overline{\varphi_i})=\pi_P(\overline{B^-s_iB^+/B^+}\cap \overline{B^+w^\bullet B^+/B^+})$. Here $\pi_P:G/B^+\rightarrow G/P$ is the canonical projection.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The local structure theorem gives the charts
\[
\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^-\cong U_P^-\times Z,\qquad
\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^+=\dot w^\bullet\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^-\cong U_P^+\times\dot w^\bullet Z,
\qquad Z\cong\mathbb A^r;
\]
see \cite{DCS99}*{Propositions~3.6 and~3.8}. The toric variety
$Z$ has open torus $\breve T_{\mathrm{ad}}$ and a fixed point $z_0$
with stabilizer $P$. Identify $Y=G/P$ by $gP\mapsto gz_0$.
Then
\[
Y\cap\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^-=B^-P/P,\qquad
Y\cap\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^+=B^+\dot w^\bullet P/P.
\]

We first prove~(1). By Theorem~\ref{thm:linebundles} and its proof,
the section $\chi_{\overline{\omega_i}}$ is defined and nowhere vanishing
on $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^-$. Thus $\dot w^\bullet\chi_{\overline{\omega_i}}$ is defined
on $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^+$ and does not vanish there.
For $x\in U_P^+$ and $t\in T$, the definition of $\varphi_i$ gives
\[
\frac{\varphi_i(x\dot w^\bullet tK)}
{(\dot w^\bullet\chi_{\overline{\omega_i}})(x\dot w^\bullet tK)}
=c_i\Delta_{\omega_i,w^\bullet\omega_i}(x),
\qquad c_i\in k^\times.
\]
Indeed, $\theta(x)^{-1}$ fixes $v_{w^\bullet\omega_i}$ and the
common torus factor is $\overline{\omega_i}(t)$. The quotient descends under
$D$ because its numerator and denominator have the same character.
It is independent of the torus coordinate, so the same formula
holds on $Y\cap\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^+$. It is nonzero whenever
$x\dot w^\bullet B^+\in\mathring{\mathcal{R}}_{e,w^\bullet}$,
a nonempty open Richardson variety. Hence
$\overline{\varphi_i}\ne0$, proving~(1).

We now prove~(2) and~(3).
For $v\le w^\bullet$, let $\mathring C_v^\pm\subset U_P^\pm$
be the Richardson loci in the unipotent coordinates of
Proposition~\ref{prop:chart-richardson}. On the adjoint open orbit,
\[
\mathring S_v\cap\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^\pm
\cong\mathring C_v^\pm\times\breve T_{\mathrm{ad}}.
\]
Keeping the unipotent coordinate fixed and taking the torus factor
to $z_0$, or to $\dot w^\bullet z_0$, gives the points $xP$, or
$x\dot w^\bullet P$, in $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_v\cap Y$. Taking closures in $Y$ yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pip}
\pi_P(\mathcal{R}_{w_\bullet,vw_0})\subseteq\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_v\cap Y,
\qquad
\pi_P(\mathcal{R}_{\kappa(v),w^\bullet})\subseteq\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_v\cap Y.
\end{equation}
Since $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_{s_{\kappa(i)}}\subseteq Z(\varphi_i)$, these inclusions
immediately imply
\begin{equation}\label{eq:phi-divisor-bound}
\begin{gathered}
\operatorname{div}(\overline{\varphi_i})\ge A_i,\\
A_i:=\begin{cases}
\pi_P(\mathcal R_{s_i,w^\bullet})
+\pi_P(\mathcal R_{w_\bullet,w_0s_{\tau i}}),&i\notin \mathbf{I}_{\bullet
},\\
\pi_P(\mathcal R_{s_i,w^\bullet}),&i\in \mathbf{I}_{\bullet
}.
\end{cases}
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Here each projected Richardson variety has its reduced divisor
structure, and an empty variety contributes zero. For $i\in \mathbf{I}_{\bullet}$,
the two projected Richardson divisors coincide by
\cite{KLS14}*{Lemma~3.1}:
\[
\pi_P(\mathcal R_{s_i,w^\bullet})
=\pi_P(\mathcal R_{w_\bullet,w_0s_{\tau i}}).
\]

The $A_i$ together contain each projected Richardson divisor of
$G/P$ exactly once. Thus, by \cite{KLS14}*{Lemma~5.4},
\[
\Delta:=\sum_{i\in\mathbf{I}}A_i
=\sum_{i\in\mathbf{I}}\pi_P(\mathcal R_{s_i,w^\bullet})
+\sum_{i\notin J}\pi_P(\mathcal R_{w_\bullet,w_0s_i})
\]
is anticanonical. On the other hand,
$\overline\rho=\sum_i\overline{\omega_i}
=\rho+w_\bullet\rho=2\rho-2\rho_{\mathbf{I}_{\bullet}}$, so
\[
0\ne\prod_{i\in\mathbf{I}}\overline{\varphi_i}
\in H^0(Y,\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_{-\overline\rho}|_Y)
=H^0(Y,\omega_Y^{-1});
\]
see \cite{BK05}*{proof of Theorem~4.1.15, equation~(1)}.
Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{div}\!\left(\prod_i\overline{\varphi_i}\right)
\ge\Delta.
\]
Both divisors are anticanonical. Their difference is effective and
linearly equivalent to zero on the projective integral variety $Y$,
and hence vanishes. Therefore
$\operatorname{div}(\overline{\varphi_i})=A_i$ for every $i$.
Since the $A_i$ are reduced divisors on the smooth variety $Y$,
these equalities identify the zero schemes and prove~(2) and~(3).
head: environment

label: thm:WCsplit
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:WCsplit}
The wonderful compactification $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$ admits a $B^+$-canonical Frobenius splitting that compatibly splits each divisor $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_{s_i}$, for $i\in\mathbf{I}$, and each boundary divisor $D_i$, for $i\in\mathbf{I}_\circ'$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For each $i\in\mathbf{I}_\circ'$, Proposition \ref{prop:wc}(3) provides a
$G$-invariant section
\[
f_i\in H^0(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_{-\overline{\alpha_i}})
\]
whose zero divisor is $D_i$. Proposition \ref{prop:wc}(2) gives
\[
\sigma=\left(\prod_{i\in\mathbf{I}_\circ'}f_i\right)
\left(\prod_{i\in\mathbf{I}}\varphi_i\right)
\in H^0(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace,\omega_\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^{-1}).
\]
The character restriction is retained throughout: the second product
belongs to $E_{\overline\rho}$ under
Theorem~\ref{thm:linebundles}.

By Proposition~\ref{prop:dv}, the restriction
$\prod_i\overline{\varphi_i}$ has divisor $\Delta$, the reduced
union of all projected Richardson divisors of $Y=G/P$.
The splitting in \cite{KLS14}*{Corollary~4.3} compatibly splits
these divisors, so its section of $\omega_Y^{1-p}$ vanishes along
$(p-1)\Delta$ by \cite{BK05}*{Exercise~1.3.E.3}.
Since $\Delta$ is anticanonical by \cite{KLS14}*{Lemma~5.4},
that section is a nonzero scalar multiple of
$(\prod_i\overline{\varphi_i})^{p-1}$.
The boundary divisors of $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$ are smooth with normal crossings
and have intersection $Y$ by \cite{DCS99}*{Theorem~3.9}.
Successive adjunction along them and
\cite{BK05}*{Exercise~1.3.E.4} show that $\sigma^{p-1}$ defines
a Frobenius splitting after a nonzero scalar normalization.

By \cite{BK05}*{Proposition~1.3.11}, the zero scheme of $\sigma$
is reduced and compatibly split. Each $Z(\varphi_i)$ is therefore
reduced. Its support on the open orbit is
$S_{s_{\kappa(i)}}$. It has no boundary-divisor component:
every boundary divisor contains $Y$, whereas
$\overline{\varphi_i}\ne0$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:dv}(1).
Thus $Z(\varphi_i)=\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_{s_{\kappa(i)}}$. Since $\kappa$
permutes $\mathbf{I}$, the splitting is compatible with every $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_{s_i}$
and every $D_i$.

We verify $B^+$-canonicality directly. The left $T$-weight of
$\varphi_i$ is
\[
-\omega_i+\theta(w^\bullet\omega_i)=-\omega_i-w_0\omega_{\tau i}.
\]
Since $w_0\rho=-\rho$, their sum is zero, and $\sigma$ is
$T$-invariant. Fix a simple root subgroup $x_j(a)\subset B^+$.
The vector $v_{w^\bullet\omega_i}$ is fixed by $\theta(U^+)$, because
$\theta(B^+)=\dot w^\bullet B^+(\dot w^\bullet)^{-1}$. Hence on $S_{\mathrm{sc}}$,
\[
(x_j(a)\cdot\varphi_i)(gK)
=v_{\omega_i}^*\!\left(x_j(-a)g\theta(g)^{-1}v_{w^\bullet\omega_i}\right).
\]
The simple-root string through the lowest weight vector
$v_{\omega_i}^*\in V(\omega_i)^*$ has length
$\langle\alpha_j^\vee,\omega_i\rangle=\delta_{ij}$.
Thus this expression has degree at most $\delta_{ij}$ in $a$.
The section identifications of Theorem~\ref{thm:linebundles} are
$G$-equivariant, and the $f_i$ are $G$-invariant. Consequently,
$x_j(a)\cdot\sigma$ has degree at most one in $a$, and
$x_j(a)\cdot\sigma^{p-1}$ has degree at most $p-1$.
Under the equivariant identification
$H^0(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace,\omega_\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^{1-p})\cong\operatorname{End}_F(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace)$ of
\cite{BK05}*{Lemma~4.1.14}, these are exactly the torus-invariance
and divided-power conditions of \cite{BK05}*{Lemma~4.1.6}.
The normalized splitting is therefore $B^+$-canonical.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The splitting of $G/P$ used in \cite{KLS14}*{Corollary~4.3} is the
pushforward of the standard splitting of $G/B^+$, and is
$B^+$-canonical; see \cite{BK05}*{Theorem~4.1.15}.
The direct verification above also proves canonicality on $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$
without lifting a map through restriction to the closed orbit.
head: environment

label: cor:si
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:si}
(1) For $i\in\mathbf{I}$, the zero scheme $Z(\varphi_i)$ is reduced and
\[
Z(\varphi_i)=\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_{s_{\kappa(i)}},\qquad
\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_{s_{\kappa(i)}})\cong\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_{-\overline{\omega_i}}.
\]

(2) $\cup_{i\in\mathbf{I}}(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_{s_i}\cap G/P)$ is the union of all projected Richardson divisors of $G/P$.

label: lem:embeddings-toroidal-map
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:embeddings-toroidal-map}
Let $X$ be a nonsingular complete toroidal embedding of $S$. Then $\pi$ extends to a $G$-equivariant morphism $\pi:X\to\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$. If $Y\subset X$ and $\ensuremath{\mathbf {Y}}\xspace\subset\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$ are closed $G$-orbits, then $\pi|_Y:Y\to\ensuremath{\mathbf {Y}}\xspace$ is an isomorphism. Moreover, if
\[
\widetilde\omega_X=\omega_X\otimes\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_X(\partial X),
\qquad
\widetilde\omega_{\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace}=\omega_{\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace}\otimes\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_{\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace}(\partial\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace),
\]
then
\[
\widetilde\omega_X\simeq\pi^*\widetilde\omega_{\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The extension of $\pi$ follows from \cite{Kno91}*{Theorem 4.1}, the assertion on closed orbits from \cite{Tan18}*{Lemma 1.2}, and the identity of logarithmic canonical sheaves from \cite{Tan18}*{Lemma 1.4}.
head: environment

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
Assume $\operatorname{char}k=p>2$, and let $X$ be an equivariant embedding of $S$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=*]
\item If $X$ is smooth, then $X$ admits a Frobenius splitting relative to
\[
(p-1)\left(\partial X+\sum_{i\in\mathbf{I}}X_{s_i}\right)
\]
that compatibly splits every boundary divisor and every stratum closure $X_u$.
\item Every equivariant embedding $X$ admits a Frobenius splitting compatible with every boundary divisor and every stratum closure $X_u$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove the two statements together. We follow the outline of \cite{Tan18}*{Proposition 2.1(i)}, using the distinguished sections of Section~\ref{sec:wonderful-splitting}. By \cite{Tan18}*{Theorem 2.1(i)}, there is a $G$-equivariant rational resolution
\[
q:\widetilde X\longrightarrow X
\]
such that $q$ is projective and $\widetilde X$ is a nonsingular quasi-projective toroidal embedding. Since $X$ is normal and $q$ is proper and birational, $q_*\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_{\widetilde X}=\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_X$. By \cite{BK05}*{Lemma 1.1.8}, a splitting of $\widetilde X$ descends to $X$, together with compatibility with the images of compatibly split subvarieties. It therefore suffices to construct the compatible splitting on $\widetilde X$; the relative assertion for smooth $X$ will follow at the end. Thus we may assume for the construction that $X$ is nonsingular, toroidal, and quasi-projective.

           
By \cite{Tim07}*{Section 29.2} or \cite{Kno91}, $X$ admits a nonsingular toroidal equivariant completion. A splitting of the completion restricts to $X$, as does compatibility with the relevant closed subschemes. We may therefore further assume that $X$ is complete. 

Lemma \ref{lem:embeddings-toroidal-map} gives a $G$-equivariant morphism $\pi:X\longrightarrow\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$.
The sections of Section~\ref{subsec:wonderful-distinguished-sections}
come from the restricting of
\[
\varphi_i\in E_{\overline{\omega_i}}
\cong H^0(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_{-\overline{\omega_i}}).
\]
By Corollary~\ref{cor:si}, their zero schemes are
$Z(\varphi_i)=\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_{s_{\kappa(i)}}$.
Put $s=\prod_{i\in\mathbf{I}}\varphi_i$. Multiplication gives
$s\in E_{\overline\rho}$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:wc} identifies
\[
\ensuremath{\mathcal {L}}\xspace_{-\overline\rho}\cong\widetilde\omega_{\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace}^{-1}.
\]
If $\ensuremath{\mathbf {Y}}\xspace\subset\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$ is the closed orbit, put $\overline s=s|_{\ensuremath{\mathbf {Y}}\xspace}$.
By Proposition~\ref{prop:dv} and the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:WCsplit}, $\overline s^{p-1}$ defines the
closed-orbit splitting after a nonzero scalar normalization.
           
By Lemma \ref{lem:embeddings-toroidal-map}, the pullback
\[
\widetilde s=\pi^*s
\]
is a section of $\widetilde\omega_X^{-1}$. Let $s_{\partial X}$ be the canonical section of $\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_X(\partial X)$ and set
\[
\sigma_X=s_{\partial X}\widetilde s\in H^0(X,\omega_X^{-1}).
\]
For every closed $G$-orbit $Y\subset X$, the restriction $\pi|_Y$ identifies $Y$ with $\ensuremath{\mathbf {Y}}\xspace$ and identifies $\widetilde s|_Y$ with $\overline s$. Hence $(\widetilde s|_Y)^{p-1}$ splits $Y$ after normalization by the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:WCsplit}.

           
The local expansion at a point of a closed $G$-orbit now shows that
\[
\sigma_X^{p-1}\in H^0(X,\omega_X^{1-p})
\]
defines a Frobenius splitting of $X$ after a nonzero scalar normalization. This is precisely the local argument in \cite{Tan18}*{Proposition 2.1(i)}; see also \cite{BK05}*{Theorem 1.3.8 and Exercise 1.3.E.4}. The factor $s_{\partial X}$ implies that every boundary divisor is compatibly split.

           
The explicit factorization of $s$ determines further compatibly split subschemes. Indeed, we have 
\[
\widetilde s=\prod_{i\in\mathbf{I}}\pi^*\varphi_i,
\]
and $Z(\sigma_X)$ is reduced and compatibly split by
\cite{BK05}*{Proposition~1.3.11}. On the open orbit, the support
of $Z(\pi^*\varphi_i)$ is $S_{s_{\kappa(i)}}$; this follows
from Corollary~\ref{cor:si} and the compatibility of the stratum
definitions with the adjoint quotient. Since $\kappa$ permutes
$\mathbf{I}$, every nonempty $X_{s_i}$ is an irreducible component of
$Z(\sigma_X)$ and is compatibly split.

We obtain compatibility with $X_u$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:prelim-strata-intersection}, standard combinatorics on Bruhat orders, and \cite{BK05}*{Proposition~1.2.1}.

                            
                                                       
                                                                  
                                                                   
                                                                
                                                                   
                                                                 
                                                          
                                                          

                                                                    
                                                                 
                                                                  
                                                                     

Finally, when $X$ is smooth, the compatible splitting is relative to
\[
(p-1)\left(\partial X+\sum_{i\in\mathbf{I}}X_{s_i}\right)
\]
by \cite{BK05}*{Theorem 1.4.10}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: For normal varieties, Frobenius splittings may be described on the regular locus using divisorial sheaves; see \cite{BK05}*{Remark~1.3.12}. Allowing effective Weil divisors, as in \cite{BK05}*{Remark~1.4.13}, Theorem~\ref{thm:main} can therefore be rephrased as the existence, for every equivariant embedding $X$, of a Frobenius splitting relative to $(p-1)\left(\partial X+\sum_{i\in\mathbf{I}}X_{s_i}\right)$, compatible with every boundary divisor and every $X_u$.

label: prop:RichardsonFregular
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:RichardsonFregular}Assume $\operatorname{char}k=p>2$. 
Richardson varieties are globally $F$-regular.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The case $v=w$ is immediate. Write
$\partial\mathcal{R}_{v,w}=\bigcup_iE_i$ as the union of its irreducible
components. The construction in \cite{KS}*{equation~(4) and
Section~4.5}, valid also in positive characteristic, gives an ample
effective Cartier divisor $D=\sum_i b_iE_i$ with $b_i>0$.
The Frobenius splitting in \cite{KS}*{Proposition~5.3}, together with
\cite{BT06}*{Lemma~3.1}, shows that $\mathcal{R}_{v,w}$ is stably
Frobenius split along $D$.
The complement $\mathring{\mathcal{R}}_{v,w}$ is smooth, hence strongly $F$-regular by \cite{HH89}*{Theorem~3.1(c)}.
The proposition follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:gloFre}(2).
head: environment

label: prop:DBFregular
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:DBFregular}
Assume $\operatorname{char}k=p>2$. For $w\le w^\bullet$, the coordinate ring $k[S_w]$ is strongly $F$-regular.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that strong $F$-regularity is local by
\cite{HH89}*{Theorem~3.1(a)}. On each nonempty chart, the stratum $\mathring{S}_{vw_0}$ is
smooth by Lemma~\ref{lem:prelim-strata-intersection}, hence strongly
$F$-regular by \cite{HH89}*{Theorem~3.1(c)}.
Moreover,
\[
\bigcup_{w\leq u\leq w^\bullet}\mathring{\mathcal{R}}_{v,uw_0}
=\mathcal{R}_{v,ww_0}\cap\mathring{\mathcal{B}}^{v}
\]
is an open subset of the Richardson variety $\mathcal{R}_{v,ww_0}$,
so it is strongly $F$-regular by
Proposition~\ref{prop:RichardsonFregular} and
\cite{BT06}*{Section~3}.
By the isomorphism \eqref{eq:atlas2}, each chart of $S_w\dot w_\bullet$
is a product of these two strongly $F$-regular varieties,
and is therefore strongly $F$-regular.
These charts cover $S_w\dot w_\bullet$.
By locality, $k[S_w]$ is strongly $F$-regular.
head: environment

label: prop:AmpleDiv
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:AmpleDiv}
Assume that $\operatorname{char}k\neq2$. Let $X$ be a smooth projective
toroidal embedding of the symmetric space $S$, with boundary divisors
$D_1,\dots,D_n$. Then there exist positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_n$ such
that $\sum_{i=1}^n a_iD_i$ is an ample effective Cartier divisor.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$ be the wonderful compactification of $S_{\mathrm{ad}}$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:embeddings-toroidal-map}, the canonical map
$S\to S_{\mathrm{ad}}$ extends to a $G$-equivariant morphism
\[
\pi:X\longrightarrow\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace.
\]
The local structure results used below apply to symmetric spaces in
characteristic different from $2$; see \cite{DCS99}*{Proposition~3.8 and
Theorem~3.9} and \cite{Tan18}*{Section~3, pp.~502--503}.

Choose the standard affine chart $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_0=\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace^-\subseteq\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$ of
Section~\ref{subsec:wonderful-closed-orbit}. The compatible
local structure theorems give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ample-boundary-chart}
\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_0\simeq U\times\ensuremath{\mathbb {A}}\xspace^{r_{\mathrm{ad}}},
\qquad
X_0:=\pi^{-1}(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_0)\simeq U\times Z,
\end{equation}
where $U=U_P^-$, $r_{\mathrm{ad}}$ is the rank of
$S_{\mathrm{ad}}$, and $Z$ is a toric variety with dense torus
$\breve T$ whose fan is the fan of $X$. The boundary divisors of $X$
correspond bijectively to the torus-invariant prime divisors
$Z_1,\dots,Z_n$ of $Z$, with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ample-boundary-components}
D_i\cap X_0=U\times Z_i.
\end{equation}
For the equality of fans and the boundary correspondence, see
\cite{Tan18}*{Lemma~1.2(i)}; the inverse-image description in
\eqref{eq:ample-boundary-chart} is used in
\cite{Tan18}*{proof of Theorem~2.1(i), p.~501}.
The $G$-translates of $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_0$ cover $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$.

Since $Z$ is closed in the open subvariety $X_0$ of the projective
variety $X$, it is quasiprojective. A quasiprojective toric variety
has an effective ample Cartier divisor supported on its toric boundary:
this follows from the invariant-divisor description of its Picard group
and the character decomposition of global sections in
\cite{CLS11}*{Theorem~4.2.1 and Proposition~4.3.3}, applied to a very
ample line bundle. These descriptions are valid over any algebraically
closed field; the same consequence is used in
\cite{Tan18}*{proof of Theorem~2.1(i), p.~501}.
Choose such a divisor
\[
E_Z=\sum_{i=1}^n b_iZ_i,\qquad b_i\in\ensuremath{\mathbb {Z}}\xspace_{\geq0},
\]
and set $E=\sum_i b_iD_i$. Since $X$ is smooth, $E$ is Cartier.
By \eqref{eq:ample-boundary-components},
\[
\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_X(E)|_{X_0}\simeq\operatorname{pr}_Z^*\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_Z(E_Z).
\]
This sheaf is ample, since $\operatorname{pr}_Z:U\times Z\to Z$ is
affine and pullback by an affine morphism preserves ampleness
\cite{Stacks}*{Tag~0892(2)}. Since $E$ is $G$-stable and
$\pi^{-1}(g\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_0)=gX_0$, its restriction to $\pi^{-1}(g\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace_0)$ is
ample for every $g\in G(k)$. Relative ampleness is local on the base
\cite{Stacks}*{Tag~01VJ}; hence $E$ (on $X$) is $\pi$-ample.

We next choose an ample effective Cartier divisor $H$ on $\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$ whose
support is $\partial\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace$. Use the projective realization
\[
\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace=\overline{G_{\mathrm{ad}}\cdot[h]}
\subseteq\ensuremath{\mathbb {P}}\xspace\bigl(\operatorname{Hom}_k({}^{\theta_{\mathrm{ad}}}V,V)\bigr)
\]
of \cite{DCS99}*{construction preceding Lemma~3.4 and Theorem~3.9}.
The open orbit consists of invertible maps, while every boundary point
represents a singular map; this is stated in
\cite{DCS99}*{proof of Theorem~3.9(ii), p.~287}.
Here ${}^{\theta_{\mathrm{ad}}}V$ is the twist of $V$ by
$\theta_{\mathrm{ad}}$, and $h$ is the canonical linear isomorphism.
Thus the determinant restricts to a nonzero section
$\delta\in H^0(\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace(d))$, where $d=\dim V$, and
\[
H=\operatorname{div}_{\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace}(\delta),
\qquad
\operatorname{Supp}(H)=\partial\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace,
\qquad
\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace(H)\simeq\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_\ensuremath{\mathbf {X}}\xspace(d).
\]
In particular, $H$ is an ample effective Cartier divisor.

The pullback $\pi^*H$ is an effective Cartier divisor, since its defining
section is nonzero on the dense open orbit $S$. Its support is contained
in $\partial X$, because $\pi(S)\subseteq S_{\mathrm{ad}}$.
Since $E$ is $\pi$-ample and $H$ is ample, there exists an integer
$N\geq0$ such that
\[
A=E+N\pi^*H
\]
is ample by \cite{Stacks}*{Tag~0892(1)}. Hence
$A=\sum_i c_iD_i$ with $c_i\in\ensuremath{\mathbb {Z}}\xspace_{\geq0}$.

It remains to make every coefficient of $A$ positive. Put $\Delta=\sum_iD_i$,
which is Cartier because $X$ is smooth. For $m\gg0$, the sheaf
$\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_X(\Delta+(m-1)A)$ is globally generated
\cite{Stacks}*{Tag~01Q3(7)}. Tensoring with the ample sheaf
$\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_X(A)$ shows that $\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_X(\Delta+mA)$ is ample
\cite{Stacks}*{Tag~0890}. Therefore
\[
D=\Delta+mA=\sum_{i=1}^n(1+mc_i)D_i
\]
is an ample effective Cartier divisor with all coefficients strictly
positive, as required.

label: thm:global-f-regular-strata
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:global-f-regular-strata}
Assume that $\operatorname{char}k=p>2$. Let $X$ be a projective
equivariant embedding of $S$. Then $X_u$ is globally $F$-regular for
every $u\leq w^\bullet$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose first that $X$ is smooth and toroidal. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:AmpleDiv}, there is an ample effective Cartier
divisor
\[
D=\sum_{i=1}^n a_iD_i,\qquad a_i>0,
\]
with $\operatorname{Supp}(D)=\partial X$. Let $\varphi$ be the
splitting constructed in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. It splits $X$
relative to $(p-1)\partial X$ and compatibly splits every $X_u$.
Iterating this relative splitting gives a stable splitting along
$(p^e-1)\partial X$. Choose $e$ such that $a_i\leq p^e-1$ for all
$i$, and restrict along
\[
\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_X(D)\hookrightarrow\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_X((p^e-1)\partial X).
\]
We obtain a stable splitting along $D$ whose induced Frobenius
splitting still compatibly splits every $X_u$; see
\cite{BT06}*{Lemma~3.1(4)--(5)} and
\cite{BK05}*{proof of Lemma~1.4.11}.

Since $X_u$ meets $S$, it is not contained in $\operatorname{Supp}(D)$.
Consequently, $D|_{X_u}$ is an ample effective Cartier divisor, and
the stable splitting descends to a stable splitting of $X_u$ along
$D|_{X_u}$ by \cite{BK05}*{Proposition~1.4.3}, applied to the
iterated Frobenius. Moreover,
\[
X_u\setminus\operatorname{Supp}(D|_{X_u})=X_u\cap S=S_u,
\]
which is strongly $F$-regular by 
Proposition~\ref{prop:DBFregular}. Theorem~\ref{thm:gloFre}(2)
therefore implies that $X_u$ is globally $F$-regular.

For an arbitrary projective embedding $X$, choose a projective
$G$-equivariant resolution
\[
q:\widetilde X\longrightarrow X
\]
with $\widetilde X$ smooth and toroidal, as in
\cite{Tan18}*{Theorem~2.1(i)}. Then $\widetilde X$ is projective and
$q_*\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_{\widetilde X}=\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_X$, since $X$ is normal. Let
$\widetilde X_u$ be the closure of $S_u$ in $\widetilde X$, and write
$q_u:\widetilde X_u\to X_u$ for the restriction of $q$. The preceding
argument gives a stable splitting of $\widetilde X$ along an ample
effective Cartier divisor supported on $\partial\widetilde X$,
compatible with $\widetilde X_u$. Since this divisor does not contain
$\widetilde X_u$, \cite{BT06}*{Lemma~3.2} gives
\[
(q_u)_*\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_{\widetilde X_u}=\ensuremath{\mathcal {O}}\xspace_{X_u}.
\]
The variety $\widetilde X_u$ is globally $F$-regular by the smooth
toroidal case. Hence $X_u$ is globally $F$-regular by
\cite{BT06}*{Corollary~3.2}.

label: cor:strong-f-regular-strata
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:strong-f-regular-strata}
Assume that $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic $p>2$.
Let $X$ be an equivariant embedding of $S$. Then $X_u$ is strongly
$F$-regular for every $u\leq w^\bullet$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Sumihiro's theorem \cite{Bri17}*{Theorem~1 and Corollary~2.14},
$X$ has a finite $G$-stable open cover by equivariant embeddings
which are open subvarieties of projective equivariant embeddings.
As in \cite{BT06}*{proof of Corollary~4.2}, the assertion follows
from Theorem~\ref{thm:global-f-regular-strata} and the locality of
strong $F$-regularity \cite{HH89}*{Theorem~3.1(a)}.
head: environment

label: thm:characteristic-zero-f-regular
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:characteristic-zero-f-regular}
Let $X$ be an equivariant embedding of $S$. Then $X_u$ is of
strongly $F$-regular type for every $u\leq w^\bullet$.
If $X$ is projective, then each $X_u$ is of globally $F$-regular type.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In the work \cite{BS24}*{Theorems~4.4 and~4.8}, we construct an integral form of $k[S]$ whose base change
to every algebraically closed field of characteristic different
from $2$ is the coordinate ring of the corresponding symmetric
space.
This provides the integral homogeneous space needed for the
reduction argument used
in \cite{HT07}*{proof of Theorem~9.1}.
We omit the remaining details.
head: environment

label: cor:characteristic-zero-singularities
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:characteristic-zero-singularities}
Let $X$ be an equivariant embedding of $S$. Then $X_u$ is normal,
Cohen--Macaulay, and has rational singularities for every
$u\leq w^\bullet$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:characteristic-zero-f-regular}, each $X_u$ is of
strongly $F$-regular type, hence of $F$-rational type by definition; see \cite{Smi97} for the definition of $F$-rationality. 
The assertion
follows from \cite{Smi97}*{Theorem~4.3}.
